title: Simplified evaluation of energetic complementarity based on monthly average data
author: Beluco, Risso, et al.

steps.title: Define complementarity objectives
steps.instruction: Decide which complementarity components to evaluate (complete complementarity or specific components such as time‑complementarity, energy‑complementarity, amplitude‑complementarity) and whether raw, final or other qualified data will be used.

steps.title: Select equal‑length data series
steps.instruction: Choose monthly average data series for the two energy resources that have the same length; note that short series may over‑estimate extreme events and that using data related to final energy supplied by plants reduces speculation.

steps.title: Find month of minimum for resource 1
steps.instruction: Identify the month (1–12) in which the first energy resource has its lowest availability and record it as m1.

steps.title: Find month of minimum for resource 2
steps.instruction: Identify the month (1–12) in which the second energy resource has its lowest availability and record it as m2.

steps.title: Calculate time‑complementarity κt
steps.instruction: Compute κt using the two equations κt = |m1 ‑ m2| and κt = m2 ‑ m1 + 12 × 6; select the smaller of the two results as the time‑complementarity index (values range from 0 for identical months to 1 for a 6‑month gap).

steps.title: Determine average availability values
steps.instruction: Calculate the mean monthly availability of the first resource (e1) and of the second resource (e2).

steps.title: Compute energy‑complementarity κe
steps.instruction: Use the equation κe = (1 ‑ e1 ‑ e2) / (e1 + e2) to obtain the energy‑complementarity component (κe = 1 when e1 = e2, κe → 0 when one mean dominates).

steps.title: Determine amplitude of variation
steps.instruction: For each resource, calculate the amplitude d as the difference between its maximum and minimum monthly availability (d1 for resource 1, d2 for resource 2).

steps.title: Calculate amplitude‑based κa
steps.instruction:
Compute δ1 = 1 ‑ d1/e1 and δ2 = 1 ‑ d2/e2. Then obtain κa using the piecewise formulas:
- If δ1 ≤ δ2: κa = 1 ‑ δ1 ‑ δ2²
- If δ1 ≥ δ2: κa = 1 ‑ δ2 ‑ δ1²
(The result ranges from 0 to 1, with κa = 1 when d1 = d2).

steps.title: Compute overall complementarity κ
steps.instruction: Multiply the three partial indexes: κ = κt × κe × κa. The final complementarity index lies between 0 (no complementarity) and 1 (full complementarity).
